To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
new TBBi derivatives are potent inhibitors of CK2 and have a significant antiproliferation effect against cancer cells.
new TBBi and TBBt derivatives bearing azide or triazole group were synthesized and their in vitro antiprotiferative and kinase profile was determined.
the new TBBi derivatives, especially compounds 7 and 10, exhibited the most potent CK2 inhibitory activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new compounds that are more potent and selective than the reference compound TBBi and may serve as a basis for the development of more effective anticancer agents.
the synthesis and evaluation of new benzimidazoles and benzotriazoles as CK2 inhibitors.
the synthesis of new derivatives of benzimidazole and benzoazole and their evaluation as potential CK2 inhibitors with antiproliferation activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most potent inhibitors of CK2 were the TBBi derivatives substituted with triazole group.
the most potent inhibitors of the CK2α activity are compounds with carboxyl or amino substituents on the triazole ring.
new TBBi derivatives have demonstrated the potential to be developed as a novel class of CK2 inhibitors with antiproliferation activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new TBBi derivatives are promising CK2 inhibitors with potential anticancer activity.
the new TBBi derivatives have a potential to be developed into a new generation of selective CK2 inhibitors with a broad spectrum of biological activity.
the TBBi derivatives bearing azide or triazole group are promising candidates for anticancer drug development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of azido and triazole groups to the TBBi structure led to the compounds with high inhibitory potential against CK2.
the introduction of a carboxyl group in the triazole ring of the TBBt derivative resulted in a significant improvement in the activity against CK2.
TBBi derivatives bearing azide or triazole groups may be promising CK2 inhibitors.
